A.explanation: Time period is correct for gap 1, but amplitude is the maximum displacement and is the same for the whole wave, not the equal vertical values at X and Y.

B.explanation: The time axis means one repeat in time is the time period $T$, and X and Y are at the same height on the displacement axis so have equal displacements.

C.explanation: Wavelength is measured on a displacement-distance graph, not a displacement-time graph, and amplitude does not describe the equal values at X and Y.

D.explanation: X and Y do have equal displacements, but the horizontal separation on a time axis cannot be wavelength which is a length in $\text{m}$.

hints: Look at the axis labels: the horizontal axis is time and the vertical axis is displacement for one fixed point, with X and Y joined by a horizontal dashed line.
Recall that the time for the motion at one point to repeat exactly is the time period $T$, while wavelength $\lambda$ is a distance and needs a displacement against distance graph.
Compare the vertical positions of X and Y with the peak height: the peak height is the amplitude, whereas the common height of X and Y is their instantaneous displacement.
walkthrough: Identify the graph type: it is displacement against time for a single point on the string, so any horizontal interval is a time interval in $\text{s}$, not a distance.
Recall the rule: the time for one complete oscillation at a fixed point is the time period $T$. On this trace one full sine cycle from X to the same stage of motion is one period.

Check separation XY: X is on the falling part of the first cycle and Y is on the falling part of the next cycle at the same stage, so XY spans exactly one repetition. Therefore gap 1 is time period, not wavelength.
Compare X and Y vertically: the dashed line shows they have the same distance from the equilibrium $0$ line, so they have the same instantaneous displacement.
Distinguish from amplitude: amplitude is the maximum displacement given by the height of the crests, which is constant for the wave but is not what is equal specifically at X and Y.
Thus gap 1 is time period and gap 2 is displacements. This is option B.
